checkpoints.description: [1/3] Plan: fit tall chambers to the desktop viewport with a pure, tested width calculation and a played Confluence run

impact_assessment.why: The Confluence is an 11x23 board: at 1440x900 its frame renders 1297px tall (bottom 1484), so 45% of the relay is below the fold and the player cannot see both ends of a beam while rotating pieces.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every chamber fits the visible game area at desktop sizes; The Confluence drops from 1297px to about 330px wide and 650px tall, with 26px cells still above the dense-cell floor; the remaining width goes to whitespace instead of hidden tiles.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: board width is inline-styled, so resize and screen changes must recompute; dependency: none, pure arithmetic module; concurrency: none; state: no save change; mobile keeps horizontal fit and a 24px cell floor for coarse pointers.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure fitBoardWidth() unit-tested across tall/square/short cases, computed from measured frame top and CSS padding; apply after every renderBoard and on resize; verify 18 boards across 1440x900, 1280x720 and 390x844 with Playwright geometry, plus a full 13-move Confluence playthrough.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented: pure fitBoardWidth module with six failing-first tests, desktop board fit on render/resize/screen return, README and ADR-009; no engine, level, save or UI-handle change

[3/3] Verified: npm test 62/62; aikit check 5/5; 18/18 scripted browser runs at exact par and 3 stars, 0 console errors; The Confluence fits 1440x900 (334x657) and improves 1280x720 (304 wide, 57px board overflow); before/after pairs captured; checklists: passed
Task 'cycle-01-board-fit' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: give beam-state changes audible feedback with a pure cue decision, a receiver-charge chime, and the dead portal cue wired to real transits

impact_assessment.why: A played run shows the core progress events are silent: rotating a mirror that charges a receiver on Split Decision plays only the 660Hz rotate click, and flipping the Detour splitter that changes the portal transit plays only the splitter pair, even though audio.js already ships playPortal() unused. The player hears the action but not what it did.
impact_assessment.benefits: Receiver progress and portal transits become audible without new assets or dependencies; the existing synthesized portal cue stops being dead code; action and consequence sounds layer instead of replacing each other.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: cellNear moves from app.js into the pure engine; dependency: none, WebAudio only; concurrency: several tones can start in one gesture, so gains must stay low; state: no save change, no visual or inventory change; tests run without AudioContext.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure feedbackFor/portalTransitKey module with unit tests, engine-level cellNear tests, a two-note charge at low gain, and a Playwright run that counts actual oscillator frequencies before and after one real click on Split Decision, Detour and Wormhole.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Implemented: engine-level cellNear export, pure cues module (portalTransitKey/feedbackFor) with 10 tests, two-note playCharge, app wiring for charge and portal consequence cues, README and ADR-010

[3/4] Verified: npm test 73/73; aikit check 5/5; real clicks add 880/1318.5Hz on receiver charge and 330/660Hz on portal transit while no-change rotations stay silent; 18/18 levels still solved at par; checklists: passed
Task 'cycle-02-audio-feedback' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: make live portal pairs legible with four pair colors, a live glow ring, and a pure live-pair helper driven by the beam trace

impact_assessment.why: Portal gates are rendered at identical full brightness whether or not the beam uses them, and pairs 1, 2 and 4 share the same lime. In Long Way Home pair 1 carries the beam and pair 3 is idle, yet all four gates glow the same; in The Confluence active pair 2 is indistinguishable from idle pairs 1 and 4.
impact_assessment.benefits: Players can read which pair is live at a glance, and four gate pairs get four colors (lime, cyan, magenta, gold) instead of two; this supports the multi-pair Episode IV chambers without changing rules or levels.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds visual state classes only, no UI handles; dependency: none; concurrency: one class toggle per portal on the existing trace; state: no save change; color contrast and forced-colors must stay legible.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure livePortalPairs() unit-tested against Long Way Home, The Confluence and an unused-pair level; class toggling reuses the existing traceBeams paths; screenshots from identical state and viewport; forced-colors rule and reduced-motion animation; a real click on The Confluence proves the live set moves.

checkpoints.description: [2/4] Implemented: pure livePortalPairs helper with three tests, is-live toggle plus beam-passing aria label, four pair colors, idle dim/live ring, forced-colors and reduced-motion handling, README and ADR-011

[3/4] Verified: npm test 76/76; aikit check 5/5; Long Way Home and Confluence before/after pairs show live vs idle gates; real splitter flip moves live set [2,2] to [1,1,2,2] and the 13-move clear lights all four pairs; 18/18 levels still at par; checklists: passed
Task 'cycle-03-portal-legibility' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: keep the par target visible on compact HUDs and pluralize the one-move hint with a pure helper

impact_assessment.why: At max-width 520 the HUD hides .metric em, the only par target on the game screen; a 390px phone shows MOVES 0 and RECEIVERS 0/2 but no par, and splitter/portal levels do not repeat it in the hint. First Light also reads 'Par is 1 moves.'
impact_assessment.benefits: Par remains visible from 320px up, the metric wraps instead of disappearing, and one-move copy reads correctly; no new HUD row or handle is needed.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: style rule removal and a new hint helper; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: no save change; at 320px the metrics bar grows 3px and the move metric wraps its par line.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure parHint() cases for 1/4/13/invalid, a stylesheet guard against re-hiding .metric em, mobile before/after screenshots at 390x844, a 320x568 overflow check, a 4-tap Double Down clear and the full 18-chamber regression run.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented: removed the compact .metric em hide, added pure parHint() with singular/plural copy, wired it into the game hint, added three hint tests and a stylesheet guard, README and ADR-012

[3/3] Verified: npm test 80/80; aikit check 5/5; 390x844 HUD shows /4 par with no overflow, 320x568 wraps cleanly, 4-tap Double Down clear at 4 moves/3 stars, desktop hint now 'Par is 1 move.'; 18/18 levels at par; checklists: passed
Task 'cycle-04-par-visibility' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: stop an older build from overwriting a newer save version, preserving the unsupported record byte-for-byte per G-001

impact_assessment.why: G-001 says a loader refuses a version it does not support without modifying or quarantining it. Today loadProgress returns blank for version 2, then the first save normalizes and writes version 1. A played probe seeded version 2 with a FUTURE profile and futureOnly field; after one First Light clear the record became version 1, the profile reset and futureOnly vanished.
impact_assessment.benefits: A future-version save survives an older cached page or website build; the current record stays byte-for-byte intact while the game remains playable read-only in memory; corrupt records can still be replaced as before.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: saveProgress gains a refuse-to-write branch; dependency: none; concurrency: single-threaded localStorage; state: no change to v1 saves, no migration, no quarantine; a future save cannot be progressed in this build.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Two progress tests (newer version preserved, corrupt record still replaceable), a before/after Playwright probe that seeds version 2 and plays First Light, and the existing round-trip tests for v1.

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Implemented: saveProgress refuses to write when the stored record has a newer integer version, keeps corrupt records replaceable, adds newer-version and corrupt-recovery tests, README save wording and ADR-013

[3/3] Verified: npm test 82/82; aikit check 5/5; played version-2 probe keeps version 2, FUTURE profile and futureOnly byte-for-byte while First Light still clears at 3 stars; 18/18 levels at par; checklists: passed
Task 'cycle-05-future-save' completed successfully.
